lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The first shifted street they found together was almost polite about it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It began as an ordinary alley behind a row of dye-works in the lower western district. The morning air there tasted of copper, vinegar, and wet wool. Strips of dyed cloth hung from upper windows, dripping red and indigo onto the packed earth below. Workers moved between vats with their arms stained to the elbow, shouting measurements at one another over the hiss of boiling water.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By the time Zeek and the others reached the middle of the alley, the noise had thinned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The bricks darkened from sun-baked brown to a nearly black clay that held a faint sheen beneath the grime. The air cooled against Zeek's face, carrying the mineral smell of sealed stone and standing water. Behind them, a dye-worker cursed as someone spilled a vat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The voice sounded much farther away than it should have.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Where the alley ought to have ended against the back of a warehouse, it simply continued—a narrow descending passage that none of the city maps recorded and none of the locals would admit existed when asked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stopped at the change in the masonry and tested the ground with the butt of his spear.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: It wasn't here when we turned the corner,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She was already examining the join where new brick met old. The seam did not look built. It looked grown. One wall belonged to a warehouse raised within living memory. The other had been worn smooth by hands that had not touched it in centuries.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun had her stylus out before the rest of them finished speaking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She pressed a damp clay tablet against her forearm and began copying the seam with the focused intensity of someone who had waited years for the city to make a mistake she could catch in writing.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: So we can arrest it later.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: So when the alley disappears, one of us possesses proof it existed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo leaned closer to the bricks.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: This city seems fond of exceptions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stood back and watched the three of them settle into the work without discussion.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The division of labor had formed in less than a day and no one had needed to declare it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, the alley remained open. A blue length of cloth stirred above the entrance. Beyond it, people moved across the ordinary street without looking in. One man stopped near the mouth of the alley, adjusted a jar against his hip, and continued walking as if four people had not just vanished into a passage where no passage belonged.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek took a length of chalk from his pouch and drew a short line across the bricks at shoulder height.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: So we know whether the wall moves?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: So we know whether we do.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg gave the dark passage another look.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They moved in the order that was already becoming habit: BAH-lahg first, En-HEH-doo second, Ninsun third, Zeek last.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The walls narrowed until shoulders brushed stone. The temperature dropped with every dozen steps. Somewhere ahead water dripped with the slow patience of a place that had never needed to hurry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then fourteen down a slope so gradual he felt it more in his knees than saw it beneath his feet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At the twenty-seventh step, the noise of the dye-works disappeared completely.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A long horizontal crack ran through three courses of the left wall. Not fresh. Not old enough to ignore.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg pressed the end of his spear against the lowest brick and leaned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun spoke before Zeek could move.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The mortar's different there. See the color? That's not the same mix as the rest of the wall. Someone patched it once already and did a bad job.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at her, then at the crack.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The repair was older than the settling, and the original workman had used a weaker lime. Worse, the patch had been laid over soot.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He scraped at the edge with his awl.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A thin black layer came away.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo turned from the passage ahead.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Long enough for someone to rebuild over it. Not long enough for the soot to wash out of the joints.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked up at the low ceiling.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek set his pack against the opposite wall and removed a short timber, a wedge, and a coil of cord. The timber had been cut for tent work, not masonry, but the grain ran straight and the wood was dry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He positioned it beneath the weakest section.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg held the upper end while Zeek drove the wedge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wall gave a low grinding sound.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The crack widened by the thickness of a fingernail.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You fixing it or persuading it to kill us faster?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek adjusted the angle, drove the wedge again, and tested the pressure until the crack stopped complaining.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek wiped the dust from his hands.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Things that aren't fixed have a habit of falling on whoever's standing under them. I prefer the people standing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo's voice drifted back from farther up the passage.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Some of us prefer the people paying.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Some of us prefer the ceiling staying where the builders put it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun touched the repaired mortar with the end of her stylus.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I noticed you noticed the mortar.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Good. I'd hate to misrecord it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The passage widened just enough for BAH-lahg to lower his spear. The floor changed beneath their boots. Packed earth became fitted stone, each slab cut in a long narrow rectangle and laid with a precision the city above no longer bothered to imitate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: At first he saw only scratches. Then the pattern resolved.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Parallel grooves ran along the edges of the slabs, shallow but regular.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The light caught a second set of grooves crossing the first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek ran two fingers through the nearest channel.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: No wheel hubs. No hoof cuts.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Something heavy was moved through here repeatedly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's gaze went toward the darkness ahead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun copied the pattern onto her tablet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo stood and dusted her hands.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Maybe the stone was quarried somewhere below and brought up.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Then the edges would be chipped,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked down at the grooves.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Something the builders expected to move again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A drop of water struck the floor ahead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sound did not echo correctly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg heard it too. His grip shifted on the spear.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek crouched and pressed his palm flat against the stone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen warmed at once.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That is becoming a very specific kind of nothing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg planted the butt of his spear beside Zeek's boot.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Excellent. We've reached the part where everyone lies.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek ignored him and tapped the floor with the bronze awl.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He moved six inches and tapped again.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This far beneath the flood channel?

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: That would be a bad place for one.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: So naturally the city built it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tapped farther along the slab.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The hollow space followed the passage.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Good. I worried the invisible corridor under our feet might complicate things.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: That is not a complication. That is knowledge.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: For you, those are usually the same thing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo covered a laugh with a cough.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The passage ended in a small square chamber that should not have existed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Its proportions were wrong for storage and too cramped for worship. A single doorway had been blocked with bricks of several different ages. The faded remains of a painted boundary stone had been set into the floor, its upper surface worn nearly smooth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun went straight to the stone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg tested the blocked door with the flat of his hand and shook his head.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: No. Doorway's older than the fill.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stayed near the entrance and listened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The city was quiet in the particular way it became when it was paying attention.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Only the slow drip of water and the faint scrape of Ninsun's stylus against clay.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She crouched over the boundary stone, brushing grit from its edges.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: This district used to have a different name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Every copy of the tablet that should have held it is blank.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo, still crouched in the far corner, held up a small flat piece of bronze she had worked free from the dirt.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was a broken seal impression, the kind used on private contracts. Green corrosion covered one edge. The symbol in the center was only half there, but the remaining curve matched the spiral-drop on Zeek's palm exactly.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned it so the others could see.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Whoever sealed this place the first time used the same mark you're carrying.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun crossed the room and took the bronze carefully by its edges.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun angled it toward the lamp.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The border is doubled. Private contracts used a single line. Temple inventories used three.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: So this belonged to a civic office.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun wiped the bronze gently with the edge of her sleeve.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I recognize what it might be.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I dislike sentences built that way.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun pointed to the surviving wedge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked toward the blocked doorway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek studied the brick fill. The oldest courses were near the edges. The center had been rebuilt several times, each layer set over the last rather than removing it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He crossed the chamber and pressed his ear to the bricks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then a low sound moved through the wall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Too large to belong to anything standing on the other side of a doorway.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Walls don't make you look like that.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo came beside him and placed two fingers against the bricks.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun was still examining the seal.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We need a rubbing of the boundary stone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun moved quickly. She placed a thin sheet of damp parchment across the painted stone and rubbed charcoal over the surface.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then pale lines emerged beneath the black.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Four streets arranged around a central square.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The chamber they occupied was marked at the edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beneath it, another shape had been drawn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A circle divided by seven lines.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stared at the seven divisions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath Zeek's linen burned.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The blocked doorway gave a soft knock.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She rolled the parchment at once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The third knock came from beneath their feet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Enough for a thin line of black moisture to rise between them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It moved against the slope of the floor.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They backed out the way they had come.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg went last this time, spear lowered toward the chamber. The black line followed until it reached the threshold.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Because the water had chosen to.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The braced section of wall was still holding.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek checked the timber as they passed. The wedge had sunk deeper into the mortar, though no weight pressed visibly against it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The wall wasn't cracked when we entered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She held up the clay tablet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The surface remained damp and smooth except for the first lines she had recorded near the alley entrance.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun ran her thumb over the blank section.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The sound cracked through the passage.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The floor tilted beneath them. Not collapsed—tilted, as if the passage had become the side of something much larger turning in its sleep.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek caught the wall with one hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The spiral mark flared under the linen.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For an instant the dark bricks became transparent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beyond them lay a city beneath the city.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Figures standing motionless on rooftops, all facing upward.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wall was only brick again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo grabbed Zeek by the back of his belt and pulled him onward.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Whatever you're looking at, look faster.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ordinary alley waited ahead, bright with daylight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg crossed first. Ninsun followed, clutching the rubbing and her tablet to her chest. En-HEH-doo pushed Zeek through just as something struck the passage behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The impact sent cold air across his back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then the sound of the dye-works crashed over them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A donkey kicked at a tether post.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The narrow descending passage was gone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The warehouse wall stood where it should have been.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His chalk line remained on the brick.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg bent over with his hands on his knees.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun stared at her clay tablet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: So had the plan of the chamber.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Beneath it, new marks pressed themselves into the wet clay.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun read it once and went pale.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She turned the tablet toward him.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The signs were old but legible.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: THE MOUTH REMEMBERS WHAT THE CITY FORGETS.
lines.note: Written text (ledger/inscription/journal, not in Bel-iddin's hand). Cold, deliberate read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Below the sentence, another line appeared.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo fell into step beside Zeek when they started walking again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Assuming she doesn't get us all killed chasing blank tablets.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun, walking ahead with BAH-lahg, did not turn around.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked at the tablet under Ninsun's arm.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I'm less worried about the scholar getting us killed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek adjusted the pack straps and kept walking.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One city that had already started rewriting the map under their feet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: And somewhere beneath the ordinary noise of Uruk, something had begun keeping its own record.
